description: Substance × Quality dimensions for the IDEAS track (ARTICULATE/INVESTIGATE/RESOLVE)
about:
The IDEAS grid maps the intellectual landscape of a decision. Each cell is an intersection of **substance** (what are we thinking about?) and **quality** (how well are we thinking about it?).

The rows capture the **building blocks of ideas**: claims, concepts, tensions, assumptions, objections, analogies — the raw material of thought. The columns capture **epistemic qualities**: how precise, how deep, how well-evidenced, how coherent each building block is.

A cell like (Core Claim × Evidence Strength) asks: "How well-supported is our central thesis?" A cell like (Objections × Completeness) asks: "Have we exhaustively considered what argues against us?"

This grid does NOT deal with execution, stakeholders, timelines, or resources — those belong to the PROCESS grid. IDEAS is purely about the quality of thinking.

conditions.name: Core Claim
conditions.description: The central thesis or proposition being advanced

conditions.name: Conceptual Definitions
conditions.description: What key terms and concepts mean in this context

conditions.name: Causal Mechanisms
conditions.description: How things connect — what drives what

conditions.name: Tensions & Contradictions
conditions.description: Where ideas pull apart or compete

conditions.name: Underlying Assumptions
conditions.description: What's taken as given, often invisibly

conditions.name: Alternative Framings
conditions.description: Other ways to see the same problem

conditions.name: Ethical Dimensions
conditions.description: Values, moral weight, fairness at stake

conditions.name: Objections & Counterarguments
conditions.description: What pushes back against the claim

conditions.name: Conceptual Dependencies
conditions.description: What must be true first for this to hold

conditions.name: Integrative Synthesis
conditions.description: How the parts form a coherent whole

axes.name: Interconnectedness
axes.description: Isolated point to integrated with other elements

axes.name: Complexity
axes.description: Simple and clean to intricate and layered

axes.name: Action Proximity
axes.description: Pure abstraction to ready for implementation

description: Operations × Execution Quality dimensions for the PROCESS track (DO/LEARN/DECIDE)
about:
The PROCESS grid maps the execution landscape of a decision. Each cell is an intersection of **operational substance** (what needs to happen?) and **execution quality** (how well-positioned are we to do it?).

The rows capture **operational concerns**: resources, timelines, dependencies, risks, stakeholders, feasibility — the practical reality of getting things done. The columns capture **execution qualities**: how urgent, how complex, how controllable, how recoverable each concern is.

A cell like (Dependencies × Complexity) asks: "How intricate are the blocking relationships?" A cell like (Stakeholder Buy-in × Urgency) asks: "How quickly do we need alignment?"

This grid does NOT deal with conceptual clarity, evidence, or argument quality — those belong to the IDEAS grid. PROCESS is purely about the quality of execution.

conditions.name: Risk Factors
conditions.description: What could go wrong in execution?

conditions.name: Learning Requirements
conditions.description: What needs to be figured out?
